objects.taxonomy_description: A toroidal pastry characterized by a central hole and typically glazed or topped.

diagnostic_checkpoints.Overall_Shape: The object exhibits a distinct toroidal geometry with a visible central hole, distinguishing it from solid round pastries like buns or bagels.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Surface_Texture: The surface is smooth and often coated with a glossy glaze, icing, or sprinkles, unlike the matte or flour-dusted finish of bread-based items.
diagnostic_checkpoints.Structural_Integrity: The item appears as a soft, leavened dough product without the flaky, layered stratification seen in croissants or puff pastries.

objects.taxonomy_description: Stringed instrument with solid or semi-hollow body (no sound hole required). Body shape varies: Stratocaster (double-cutaway, contoured edges), Les Paul (single-cutaway, carved top), Telecaster (single-cutaway, slab body). Body is wood (alder, mahogany, maple) with glossy polyester or nitrocellulose finish in solid colors, sunburst, or natural wood grain. Neck is maple or mahogany with fretted fingerboard (rosewood or maple, 21-24 frets). Pickups (magnetic, 1-3) mounted on body. Control knobs (volume, tone) and pickup selector switch. Bridge is fixed or tremolo. Headstock has 6 tuning pegs. Cable jack on body edge.

objects.taxonomy_description: Small Old World monkey measuring 30-60 cm body length weighing 2-8 kg. Body covered with long hair around face forming distinctive facial ruff. Fur coloration variable by species in gray, brown, olive, or red. Face bare with expressive features. Eyes forward-facing with brown irises. Nose narrow. Ears small. Tail long and non-prehensile. Hind limbs elongated. Body slender and agile. Inherited mammal traits include endothermy, fur insulation, mammary glands, and four-chambered heart. African arboreal monkey with complex social behavior.

Head_and_Face: Long hair around face forming distinctive facial ruff.
Body_and_Plumage: Body with variable size ranging from small to moderately large across species.
Fur coloration variable by species in gray, brown, olive, or red.
